card.name: Linking words before injury or harm
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as 'could', 'in' or 'to' right after a cause (sudden loss of consciousness, falling asleep, syncope, falls) where the next word is likely to be injury, accidents or harm.

modes.label: Result in / lead to
modes.description: The word 'in' or 'to' after 'resulted' or 'leading' that introduces accidents or injuries.
modes.example: which sometimes resulted<< in>> accidents. Although many of these patients reported

modes.label: Could cause harm
modes.description: The word 'could' after a fainting or loss-of-consciousness event, before 'cause harm' or 'result in an injury'.
modes.example: sudden loss of consciousness<< could>> cause harm to themselves or others. Consider

modes.label: Adjective before injury
modes.description: A word like 'personal' after 'serious' that directly precedes 'injury'.
modes.example: Accidentally digging into a line can cause serious<< personal>> injury as well as costly interruption of utility

card.writes: It pushes the model to predict injury words such as injury, injuries and injured next.
card.plain: It fires on the small word just before the text says someone may get hurt or have an accident.
